newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rebels set refugee ship on fire.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rebels set refugee ship on fire.

text.p: Tamil Tiger separatists forcibly boarded a ship used to ferry refugees in northwestern Sri Lanka early on Tuesday and set it on fire, naval officials said.

They said the five boats of Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) surrounded the ship at Peslai in northwestern Mannar, some 240 km (150 miles) north of the capital Colombo and reportedly abducted the crew before setting the ship on fire. Only the crew was on board at the time it was attacked by the rebels.
The rebels attacked the boat at 6.30 a.m. (1200 GMT), the officials said.

"It was a private ship which could carry 250 passengers. But at the time of the attack only the crew was on board since it was coming to Mannar to take refugees to Jaffna peninsula," one navy official told Reuters.

The LTTE are fighting for a separate homeland for minority Tamils in Sri Lanka's north and east. Government troops launched a major offensive on the rebel's northern Wanni stronghold in May to open a strategic highway linking northern Jaffna peninsula to rest of the island.
The offensive has slowed down after rebels launched two counterattacks in two weeks last month, in which scores of soldiers and separatists were reportedly killed.
